A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PartGS and provide readable text, equations, nine figures and six tables. Each contains 10 pages ending with references; neither includes an appendix. Both refer to separate supplementary material that is absent from the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original PartGS reconstruction, view-synthesis, efficiency and ablation results on DTU and ShapeNet, alongside qualitative real-scene results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and qualitative demonstrations, with revised DTU point-level reconstruction values.

M1.justification: The reported loss specification is corrected: changing D_i from 1−Ψ_i to Ψ_i−1 changes the coverage and inter-block entry penalties as written. The hybrid representation, adaptive blocks and two-stage optimization remain. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 15 DTU scenes, four ShapeNet categories with 15 objects each, BlendedMVS scenes (called BlenderMVS in the text), and self-captured scenes. Reconstruction, view synthesis, segmentation comparisons and application scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same comparator membership, including EMS, MBF, their NeuS-based variants where applicable, PartNeRF, DBW, 2DGS and Neuralangelo. Figure 6 retains OmniSeg3D and Gaussian Grouping. Newly cited GaussianBlock is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Previously stated sample counts, 30k-plus-30k training iterations, hyperparameters, metrics and ablation settings remain unchanged. The newly stated 50 ShapeNet training views and 100-fold Chamfer-distance scaling document existing experiments; neither is presented as a revision to an earlier setting.

E4.justification: Tables 5–6 and Figures 5, 7–8 retain the same loss-removal, adaptive-block, Gaussian-scale, parsimony-weight and initial-primitive-count analyses. Their numerical and visual evidence is unchanged; the revised overlap-loss interpretation adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Averaging results across objects and scenes remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises 13 of 15 DTU point-level Chamfer distances, changing the mean from 1.05 to 0.98; S24 changes from 0.95 to 0.70. Table 2 changes the point-level CD from 0.95 to 0.98. Other table results and qualitative evidence remain unchanged. No rerun is documented.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the signed-distance definition and inside/outside inequalities, resolving v2's inconsistency with the inside-point sampling condition and distance-based penalties. It also corrects D_j to D_i in the ray-crossing loss, v2 Equation 7 versus v3 Equation 6. These are limited mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract softens semantic-part parsing to interpretable decomposition and describes the framework as self-supervised. The introduction newly asserts 33.3%/75.9% reconstruction improvements, 3.18/16.13 PSNR increases and 4×/3× speedups. The central hybrid-representation and two-level reconstruction contributions persist.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 changes the interpretation of removing overlap loss from reduced semantic clarity to possible loss of small parts, using unchanged evidence. The background-free-input limitation and explanation linking large Gaussians to inconsistent depth and mesh holes are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 50 rendered training images per ShapeNet object in Section 4.1 and 100-fold scaling of reported ShapeNet Chamfer distances in Section 4.3.1. Existing training schedules, loss weights and hardware information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds SDM-Net, Neural Template, Deformer, Neural Parts and DPF-Net, acknowledging deformable shape representations. It also positions PartGS against concurrent GaussianBlock through supervision and efficiency. The Gaussian-splatting survey and Scaffold-GS references are removed; the broader positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and much of the method description are extensively rewritten, with a new title, revised terminology and recast contribution list. Section 3 reorganizes block optimization, adaptive block control and point-level decomposition into clearer subsections, including a separate Section 3.3.

P2.justification: All nine figures and six tables retain their visual examples and overall organization. Several captions are edited, including Figures 1, 2 and 6, and text and display spacing reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical consistency through the signed-distance correction and makes the experiments easier to interpret through the ShapeNet training-view count and CD scaling disclosure. Revised organization and related work also help. Gains remain limited: numerical revisions are unexplained, and Table 6 still reports default point-level CD 1.05 while Tables 1–2 report 0.98.
